note.text: A useful discussion develops a suggestion with a reason, listens to another view and reaches a practical decision. Active recall means trying to retrieve information before checking a source; rereading means looking over it again. Both can have a role, but recognising a sentence is not the same as being able to explain it unaided. This is written preparation for speaking and listening; the screen cannot assess a learner's voice or listening comprehension.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih says, I remember definitions while reading but cannot explain them later. Ayuk replies, Try closing the book and explaining one idea, then check what you missed. Bih asks, Could we practise together after chores? Ayuk agrees to alternate questions and give reasons for corrections. Their plan includes practice and feedback rather than copying answers.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: State a difficulty, suggest an action and explain why it may help. Invite a response with a specific question. When preparing a spoken exchange, write short turns and rehearse with a partner if available. Disagreement should address the method, not insult the speaker.
